title: Starting piano with Mrs. Simms and music at Tuskegee
summary: He began piano at about seven with Mrs. Simms, then violin, oboe and clarinet; all Tuskegee children studied music and played in the marching band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I'd like to digress just a minute. We've talked about Detroit and all, but when did you start piano? We hadn't discussed that.

That started at Tuskegee. I guess soon after we settled there, after my father brought my mother and Gus and me there. I started it with a wonderful woman named Mrs. Simms, who started many of the neighborhood children on piano. I guess my brother and I were probably seven and eight years old, respectively, when we started there, and of course, another thing with that school -- music study was just sort of taken for granted.

Oh, we would -- not only us, but all of the faculty that worked at Tuskegee, all the children studied music. I studied the piano, and shortly after that, I studied the violin and then later on in high school, I studied the oboe and the clarinet and worked in the marching band, played at the football games and that.

Traveled with the band, gave concerts on Sundays and march around the campus on Sunday mornings. And it was very common, it wasn't anything unusual at all -- all the kids studied music. It was just a normal part of the education.
